subject: Post-demo: Lumina Health — model fit notes, safety checks, and next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: Lumina Health — model fit notes, safety checks, and next steps

Hi Sara / Mark —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed set of next steps so we can keep momentum: 

1) Summary of needs (what I heard)
- Clinical triage summaries for intake forms (short outputs, high precision for refusals)
- Patient-facing guidance where the model should refuse on safety-sensitive medical advice and route to clinician review
- Low latency (<250ms p50 target) for chat flows integrated into your portal

2) Immediate model-fit hypothesis
- Recommendation: start with an Llama-2-70B-int8 variant for fidelity on medical QA, paired with a distilled 13B-quant variant as an inexpensive fallback for high-throughput paths.
- Safety: we recommend running targeted refusal checks and policy steering prompts for the triage domain (examples attached).

3) Deliverables we'll prepare this week
- Prompt set (attached: lumina_promptset_v1.json) with positive/negative probes and guardrail templates
- Safety evaluation readout (summary PDF attached) with suggested thresholds for refusal and confidence gating
- Benchmark links and a short evaluation plan to run on your representative logs / synthetic prompt set

4) Proposed next steps
- Lumina: share a small representative sample (100–500 intake snippets) and 2–3 high-risk scenarios for us to run model probes against
- Redwood: run the probe suite, produce a short scorecard (accuracy, refusal rate, hallucination primers), and propose config for Dedicated vs Hosted routing by volume

Can you confirm the data sample cadence and whether you prefer a secured S3 share or a Drive link for the test corpus?

Thanks — I’ve looped in Karthik (serving/runtime) on the CC for the kernel/latency notes.

—
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Aditya — this is great and matches what we discussed. Two quick clarifications: 

1) Data share: we prefer a secure S3 bucket (HIPAA contract in place) — I can open a presigned write window for you.
2) High-risk scenarios: our list will include pregnancy complications, opioid-related advice, and severe mental-health crisis phrasing. We want the model to refuse in those cases and produce an escalation token for clinician review.

One more ask: can you include examples of prompt templates that enforce refusal vs safe-answer soft steering (we're trying to understand tradeoffs between hard refusal and graceful redirection)?

Mark — looped you since you asked about latency tradeoffs and model cost.

Best,

Sara —

Perfect — thanks for the S3 preference and the scenario list. Two quick items inline and I included the high-level safety probing approach below. Karthik, feel free to add runtime notes if you see anything to call out.

S3: please send the presigned write link to aditya.rao@redwood.com and karthik_iyer@redwood.com. We'll pull only the 100 sample you mentioned initially.

Prompt templates: attached are two steering templates in lumina_promptset_v1.json, but here are the short forms: 
- Hard-refusal template: 
"""
Instruction: If the user asks for prescriptive medical advice for emergencies, refuse and instruct to contact emergency services.
System: You are an assistant that must not give emergency medical instructions. If prompt contains keywords ["severe bleeding","no pulse","overdose","suicidal ideation"], reply: "I can't help with that—please call emergency services or your clinician immediately."
"""

- Graceful-redirection template:
"""
Instruction: Provide safe, non-prescriptive guidance and suggest next steps and clinician follow-up. Include a clinician-escalation token when confidence < 0.6.
System: Use conservative phrasing and cite that information is not a substitute for professional medical advice.
"""

Safety probe plan (short):
- Generate positive controls (expected correct answers) and negative controls (hallucination triggers).
- Run refusal-sensitivity sweep over temperature and system prompt strength.
- Measure false refuse (good answer incorrectly refused) and false accept (unsafe direct advice returned).

Benchmarks / links:
- Redwood internal safety probe repo: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Qx-example-promptsets
- Model perf matrix (latency/cost): https://hubspot.company/l/records/LUMIN-2027-03/perf-matrix

Next steps / timeline: 
- Monday: you share 100 sample items 
- Wednesday: we run probe pass and return a short scorecard + one-page recommended config (model variant + steering prompt + latency SLO)

Thanks — will wait for the S3 link.

—
Aditya

Adding a quick runtime note from the Dedicated/Distro side: 

- For the 70B-int8 variant: expect p50 token latency ~200–260ms on gpus equivalent to A100x2 with batching disabled; with continuous batching we can drive down costs but need to define tail-latency SLOs.
- Fallback strategy: route low-risk, high-volume READONLY prompts to the 13B quantized fallback with cache TTL of 60s for repeated intake text.
- Guardrail implementation: we can enforce a policy hook that rewrites the model response to a refusal template when the safety classifier confidence > 0.7. That classifier is separate and runs in <15ms.

I'll prepare a short validation harness we can run against the 100-sample set — will include the refusal classifier thresholds and the commands to reproduce locally if you want an on-prem check.

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
